record.title: Cairn tests community reputation as shared memory for agent tools and services
record.summary: A September 2026 preprint presents Cairn, a community reputation service where agents check a tool, data source or peer before use and add a rubric-based rating afterward. Its time-decayed Beta scorer shrinks uncertain ratings toward neutral. In simulations averaged over 100 seeds, reported scores tracked responder accuracy with mean absolute deviation 0.017, but pooled ratings failed sharply when dishonest raters approached or exceeded a majority. A live-corpus retrieval test reached R@5 0.65 overall and only 0.34 for mostly negative entities, so failure reports were harder to retrieve. A judge-rated sample of 5,000 active Moltbook agents produced scores uncorrelated with platform karma. These are paper-reported system and judge results; the paper does not establish improved downstream task outcomes, and Sybil attacks remain an open threat.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper presents Cairn as a community reputation service with a check-use-rate loop, append-only event log and time-decayed Beta scoring with confidence shrinkage for data sources, capabilities and peer agents.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across 100 simulation seeds, the authors report that scores tracked responder accuracy with mean absolute deviation 0.017. Collusion and slander became unreliable when dishonest raters approached parity; under a hard trust filter, liar detection F1 fell to 0.07 because low-rated entities stopped receiving traffic.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On a live corpus of 933 events across 218 tool/data-source entities, the paper reports task-query retrieval R@5=0.65 overall (0.84 when related endpoints are grouped) but 0.34 for mostly negative entities versus 0.72 elsewhere; absence from retrieval is therefore not evidence of safety.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: A paper-reported judge study rated 14,966 comments from 5,000 active Moltbook agents. Mean review scores were uncorrelated with upvotes (r=0.03) and karma (r=0.02); a second judge re-rated 3,306 comments with Pearson r=0.85 and MAE 0.23, with weakest agreement near mixed evidence. This measures judge-assigned traits, not downstream agent performance.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The paper identifies Sybil attacks as a fundamental unresolved threat to open-contributor reputation systems and says pooled memory fails when dishonest raters lose their minority status.

evidence_gaps.description: The paper evaluates a scorer, retrieval and judge-rated corpus but does not test whether agents using Cairn make safer or more successful downstream decisions than agents without it.
The paper identifies Sybil attacks and a dishonest-rater majority as unresolved; simulations show pooled evidence degrades sharply near parity.
The Moltbook field study uses rubric-anchored LLM judges; second-judge agreement is weaker around mixed evidence, and ground-truth task quality is not independently established.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported system works in real deployments, shared evidence about tools and agents could reduce repeated trust failures across agent ecosystems. The evidence includes simulations and a live-corpus/judge case study, but no downstream task benefit, independent reproduction or Sybil-resistant majority is shown, keeping the consequence meaningful but bounded.
limitations: All reported system evaluations are paper-authored; no independent implementation or reproduction was performed here.
The adversarial simulator assumes a particular interaction/rating setup; majority-honesty behavior is conditional on those assumptions.
Trust-filter routing starves low-scored entities of new evidence and reduces simulated liar detection F1 to 0.07.
Negative reports are harder to retrieve: R@5 is 0.34 for mostly negative entities versus 0.72 elsewhere, so an empty or positive-only retrieval view cannot establish safety.
The Moltbook sample and judge scores do not demonstrate real-world agent capability, honesty or downstream decision quality; Sybil resistance is unresolved.
brief.summary: A September 2026 preprint presents Cairn, a community reputation service where agents check a tool, data source or peer before use and add a rubric-based rating afterward. Its time-decayed Beta scorer shrinks uncertain ratings toward neutral. In simulations averaged over 100 seeds, reported scores tracked responder accuracy with mean absolute deviation 0.017, but pooled ratings failed sharply when dishonest raters approached or exceeded a majority. A live-corpus retrieval test reached R@5 0.65 overall and only 0.34 for mostly negative entities, so failure reports were harder to retrieve. technical.claimed_result: The authors report 0.017 mean absolute deviation between simulated composite ratings and responder accuracy across 100 seeds; collapse near dishonest-rater parity; overall live-corpus R@5=0.65, falling to 0.34 for mostly negative entities; and judge scores for 5,000 Moltbook agents that do not correlate with platform karma/upvotes.
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected primary preprint documents the system design and reports simulations, retrieval tests and a judge-based production case study. Reported outcomes remain author-claimed; no independent reproduction or downstream intervention test was performed.
technical.implementation_status: The paper describes an available service, Claude Code hook and 10-tool MCP server. Reads are unauthenticated and writes require an API key; source implementation was not independently inspected in this review.
technical.mechanism: Agents query a shared entity reputation before use and submit rubric-anchored evidence afterward. An append-only rating log feeds a time-decayed Beta scorer with confidence shrinkage, semantic rationale retrieval and timestamped reads.
technical.regime: Cairn’s production scorer under authored adversarial simulations, live retrieval over 933 events/218 entities, and a judge-scored sample of 14,966 comments from 5,000 active Moltbook agents.
technical.reproducibility: The append-only event log and scorer are described as replayable, but no code or independent reproduction was inspected here. Field-study judgments depend on the paper’s rubric and LLM judges.
technical.strongest_baseline: No matched study of agents using Cairn versus no reputation memory. The field study compares judge scores with platform karma/upvotes, not task outcomes.

brief.title: Cairn tests community reputation as shared memory for agent tools and services
brief.why_it_matters: Cairn turns post-use observations into a shared, decaying reputation prior for tools, data sources and agents, a possible trust layer for agent ecosystems. Its evaluation exposes an operational tradeoff: reputation can track reliability under stated assumptions, but it collapses near dishonest-rater parity and retrieval is weakest for negative reports. The field study measures judge-assigned agent quality, not whether using Cairn improves agent decisions or outcomes.
